text.p: NASA delayed Friday's planned landing of the space shuttle Discovery at Florida's Kennedy Space Center due to a buildup of clouds.
The shuttle, which was to return from a 10-day mission to refurbish the Hubble Space Telescope, had a second opportunity to land in Florida at 3:32 a.m. EST (0832 GMT).

Flight controllers in Houston called off the planned 1:50 a.m. EST (0650 GMT) touchdown after a weather reconaissance plane noticed a buildup of cloud over the shuttle's 15,000-foot (4,572 metre) -long runway.
"We're going to have to wave off," mission control's Kevin Kregel informed the crew. "We had some low clouds formed up into a broken layer. Hopefully they will dissipate."
NASA officials were looking at the weather for the second opportunity in Florida and also at the backup landing strip at Edwards Air Force Base in California.
Discovery was to make a rare nighttime landing. Of the 82 shuttle flights, this would only be the ninth touchdown in darkness.
